# judgekeeper

> Check your LLM-as-a-judge. See how often it agrees with human labels, in one command. An LLM-as-a-judge is an AI model that grades the answers of another AI model. judgekeeper is a free, open-source command-line tool that runs on your own computer.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.judgekeeper.com/): what judgekeeper is, how to install it inside your project on Mac or Windows, and `judgekeeper start` with what it prints
- [Use it on your app](https://www.judgekeeper.com/start.html): `judgekeeper start`: what it reads, what it never does, the labeling page, the result, reviewing the disagreements, asking your judge again, trying your new judge, results saved in your own format, running it again and the install inside your project; other ways (a table you make yourself) at the end
- [With a coding assistant](https://www.judgekeeper.com/assistant.html): how to hand the job to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
- [How it works, in more depth](https://www.judgekeeper.com/learn.html): why a judge needs checking, what the numbers mean, how to keep checking, the tools it works with and a real result
- [Setup and keys](https://www.judgekeeper.com/setup.html): how to give judgekeeper an API key safely
- [Tutorial](https://www.judgekeeper.com/tutorial.html): the main commands with what each prints, on ten quiz questions
- [Your own metric](https://www.judgekeeper.com/own-metric.html): how to write your own rule, with two worked examples
- [Reference](https://www.judgekeeper.com/reference.html): every command, file format, option, exit code and config key

## For coding assistants

- [The prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/judgekeeper/judgekeeper/main/docs/assistant-prompt.md): the text a person pastes to have an assistant check their judge; it includes the rules about labels, keys and cost
